paragraphs: The 640i was the entry-level petrol variant in the BMW 6 Series range from 2011 to 2018, and it used two different engines during that run. Early cars from 2011 to 2015 use the N55 — a 3.0-litre single-turbo inline-six that was BMW's workhorse petrol engine across the range at that time. From 2015, the 640i switched to the B58, a newer-generation 3.0-litre inline-six that's a different unit entirely, not just an evolution of the N55. The B58 is the basis for many of BMW's current engines and is considered a robust design. The 6 Series was discontinued in 2018 and succeeded by the 8 Series, but we continue to rebuild and replace engines for every one still on the road.
about.boldParagraph: The 640i is no longer in production, but we continue to rebuild and replace engines for every one still on the road.

cards.body: A 3.0-litre inline-six petrol fitted to the 640i from 2011 to 2015. Generally well-regarded and reliable in this application. We replace timing chains, bearings, and gaskets as standard on every N55 rebuild.

The later 3.0-litre inline-six petrol, fitted from 2015 through the end of 6 Series production in 2018. Also well-regarded — the B58 is widely considered a robust engine with no major defect patterns in this application. We service it to the same standard as our other 640i rebuilds.

compatibility.intro: Because the 640i spans two distinct engines across its production run, fitting the wrong replacement — or assuming an N55 part will work on a B58 car — risks a compatibility problem that's expensive to unpick. Before we quote or supply anything, we confirm:

points.text: Your exact engine code (N55 or B58) via registration or VIN
Any electronics or ECU considerations specific to your exact build

compatibility.footer: This is why we always start with your registration rather than a generic 640i quote — it protects you from paying for parts that don't fit your actual car.
